subject: general
question: How do contraceptive pills help in birth control?

options.text: By preventing release of eggs from the ovary

solution:
The correct answer is **'__By preventing the release of eggs from the ovary__ '.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Contraceptive pills are** hormonal pills that prevent ovulation**.
 
• The primary mechanism of action of hormonal contraceptives is that they **suppress the secretion of gonadotropins (Follicle Stimulating Hormone, FSH and Luteinizing Hormone, LH).**
 
• The contraceptive pills **contain both progesterone and estrogen and the lower levels of estrogen** in birth control pills suppress FSH and LH, "fooling" the pituitary gland into thinking a woman is pregnant.
 
• **Ovulation will then not occur, which prevents pregnancy**.
 
• Oral contraceptive pills **do not kill sperm or ova.**
